THOUGHT: The mechanism (finger caught in a jersey and forcefully pulled) is classic for an avulsion of the flexor digitorum profundus (FDP) tendon—“jersey finger.” The key exam findings match: inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint of the ring finger and the finger resting in a more extended position, with tenderness and swelling at the DIP. X‑ray shows no fracture but soft-tissue swelling, which is consistent with a tendon avulsion without an avulsed bony fragment; MRI is appropriate to confirm the integrity and retraction of the FDP tendon. Mallet finger (terminal extensor injury) would produce an inability to extend the DIP and a drooping fingertip (flexed), which is opposite to this presentation. Thus the most likely diagnosis is an FDP avulsion (jersey finger), a condition that often requires prompt surgical evaluation for repair, especially in active young patients.
DIAGNOSIS: Jersey finger (flexor digitorum profundus tendon avulsion of the right ring finger)
ground_truth: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
